correctness.rationale: Every transitive commuting pair is a Z²/H orbit with automorphism order [Z²:H], yielding exact EGF P(z). Primitive v has exactly one containing index-m subgroup for each m; simultaneous containment corresponds to subgroups of cyclic quotient of determinant Δ and contributes FΔ. Exponential marking gives an exact bivariate law for all n. The first Rademacher term plus exponentially small remainder gives first and second partition finite-difference asymptotics; convolution by exp(FΔ) supplies multiplier exp(FΔ(1)). Exhaustive independent direct enumeration of 8,903 commuting pairs across n=1,...,6 matched 30 rational coefficient checks. Nonprimitive directions, noncommuting and independently sampled pairs excluded.

originality.rationale: Searches of published mathematical findings for simultaneous derangements, fixed-point-free primitive words, determinant overlaps, and aliases returned only different permutation statistics, with nearest IDs named. Two highly plausible same-object primary open-access articles were materially read: their variables aggregate total joint orbit counts, whereas the new theorem is a sharp exact joint law for two selected group words, including a determinant-controlled rare-event correlation. The 2026 recent logical limit-law source concerns a different sampling and signature; its full text was not accessible, recorded as risk. Partition asymptotics and exponential species counting are prior tools and not asserted novel. Best-knowledge claim-specific novelty, not uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: An older paper may specialize random finite Z²-actions to arbitrary primitive-word fixed-point counts without matching search terminology.
The accessible 2026 logical permutation-class paper was checked at abstract level only, not full text; its relevance to this different model appears limited.
These findings remain self-reviewed without independent auditing.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural dependence question among a family of elementary first-order fixed-point exclusion properties for uniformly random finite actions of Z². Although each event is rare (~n^{-1/2}), the joint probability retains a nontrivial arithmetic correlation exp(σ_{-1}(|det|)) whose value distinguishes relative positions of primitive words; it has complete exact generating functions for every finite n and a sharp asymptotic. This is structurally distinct from counting total orbits or elementary one-permutation derangements and provides a reusable arithmetic diagnostic for random action models.
